notes: Colby, 2026-09-09 12:2x, on the first take: the book went off screen mid-opening (clipping in the engine) and the strap flying off was unnecessary, 'it should just be a clasp open and then book open'. Both stills placed at 70% on a 1920x1080 magenta canvas so the opening has room; first frame = the closed book, last frame = the open spread. Seedance image-to-video with image_url + end_image_url, 6 s.

render.prompt: Static camera, no push, no zoom, no pan, one single unbroken six-second take from this one camera only. Start exactly from the first frame and end exactly on the given final frame, one continuous take without any cut; the camera never changes position, height or angle. The closed leather book, the Portfolio Handbook with its gold title, brass corners, red ribbon marker and the leather strap buckled across it, lies centred on the flat magenta plate with wide magenta on every side, exactly as in the first frame. The brass buckle unclasps and the strap falls slack, lying flat beside the book and hidden beneath it as the book opens; the strap never flies away. The front cover lifts from its right edge and swings open on its spine toward the left, the book turning to lie flat and face-on to the camera as it opens, staying centred and small enough that the whole book and its cover remain inside the frame with magenta visible around them at every moment, never touching an edge; the pages fan once and settle, until the book lies fully open as a two-page spread of blank hand-torn parchment with the stitched spine down the middle, exactly as in the final frame, and rests there for the last second. Nothing else moves; the magenta stays flat with no shadow anywhere. Layered paper cut-out craft with real material texture: worn leather, embossed gold lettering, brass corner plates and buckle, hand-torn parchment pages, soft studio light from the upper left, the book centred with wide flat magenta around it on every side, a pure, even magenta background that never changes and carries no shadow. Physics: the book stays centred and never touches or crosses any edge of the frame, the buckle unclasps before the cover lifts and the strap only falls slack and is hidden by the opening book, the cover swings on its spine like a real hinge, the pages stay bound at the spine and fan once then settle, nothing appears from nowhere and nothing leaves the frame, the magenta stays flat with no shadow anywhere, and the last frame equals the given final frame exactly. No text on the pages, no new logos.
